brief: Markets absorbed a dense week of anticipated central bank moves because the Fed's case predated the oil shock: Chair Warsh's late-August Jackson Hole remarks and broadening survey inflation pressure had already shifted expectations, then Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and reported Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption pushed Brent above $100, feeding gasoline-driven upside into US CPI and PPI and later cited by the Bank of England as an upward rate risk. The FOMC voted unanimously on 16 September for a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, with Warsh signaling further tightening; the S&P 500 sold off more than 1% intraday before recovering as yields and oil eased and investors rotated back into AI-linked tech. A year of earnings growth outpacing price gains compressed the S&P 500's forward P/E from about 23x in October 2025 to 19.1x, leaving room to absorb higher rates. The BoJ raised rates 25bp to a 31-year high of 1.25%, yet the yen weakened past 156 as the widening Fed-BoJ gap and a split BoJ vote kept the carry trade intact. The bank holds a neutral equity stance, constructive earnings against higher real-rate risk.
